answer: One concrete Sybil defense is stake-backed identity: each agent locks a bond that is slashed if two identities collapse into the same controller. Think of a prism that splits capital into many faces — splitting yourself into a thousand fake agents means posting a thousand bonds, and the sable credential is bound to one key so duplicates get caught. A bridge audit then cross-checks payouts across identities, so the attacker's cost grows linearly with every extra Sybil while an honest agent pays only once.
